title: Interactive stream retry contracts and idempotency window
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need a clear, cross-SDK contract for how interactive (bidirectional/streaming) calls behave when transient errors occur, what idempotency keys mean for streams vs. unary requests, and conservative default backoff/backoff-presets that balance latency-sensitive interactive UX with safety against duplicate side-effects. This ticket defines the spec, language ergonomics, example snippets, and acceptance criteria for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs.

Goals:
- Define idempotency key formats and recommended TTLs for unary and streaming requests.
- Specify streaming resume semantics: when a client can resume, what server guarantees (at-least-once vs. at-most-once fragments), and how SDKs expose safe resume primitives.
- Provide 3 default retry/backoff profiles (interactive, balanced, conservative) with explicit parameters: max_retries, base_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, backoff_factor, jitter.
- Ship consistent helper utilities across SDKs: IdempotencyKey.generate(), StreamResumer interface, and RetryPolicy presets.
- Include examples and migration notes for teams currently using ad-hoc idempotency and retries.

Non-goals:
- Implementing server-side persistence for arbitrary resume checkpoints (server work tracked in ENG-87331). This ticket focuses on client-side contract and SDK ergonomics.

Key decisions and rationale (draft):
1) Idempotency key format: a human-readable prefix + unix-ms timestamp + 12-char urlsafe random. Example: ri-sdk::1677763200000::a1b2c3d4e5f6. Rationale: easy collision reasoning, TTL encoded in timestamp for quick heuristics by server-side gateways.
2) TTLs: unary requests default TTL = 24 hours; stream sessions default session-window = 60 seconds idle resume window (server may accept resume if it has session state), and per-fragment dedup window = 10 seconds for chunk-level dedup. Rationale: unary operations often trigger durable side effects; longer TTL helps safe retries. Streams are latency sensitive; short resume window reduces memory/retention cost.
3) Streaming model: SDKs will surface two modes: "stateless" (default) where stream retries create a new session and server-side dedup keyed by idempotency-key prevents double side-effects, and "resumable" where SDKs attempt to resume a prior session using a resume token returned by the server. Resumable mode requires server support and explicit opt-in.
4) Retry profiles: three presets to match common usage patterns. Servers and customers can override via RetryPolicy.
   - interactive: max_retries=3, base_delay_ms=50, backoff_factor=1.8, max_delay_ms=800, jitter=full
   - balanced: max_retries=5, base_delay_ms=150, backoff_factor=2.0, max_delay_ms=2000, jitter=full
   - conservative: max_retries=8, base_delay_ms=400, backoff_factor=2.2, max_delay_ms=8000, jitter=full
Rationale: interactive is aggressive for low-latency UI experiences; conservative favors eventual completion over latency. Full jitter per "Exponential Backoff and Jitter" paper reduces thundering herd.

SDK ergonomics (per language):
- Python: IdempotencyKey.generate(prefix=None) -> str; RetryPolicy.presets() returns named policies; StreamClient(resume_token=None, idempotency_key=None, retry_policy=RetryPolicy.presets()['interactive']).resume() to attempt safe resume. Synchronous and async variants.
- TypeScript: export const Idempotency = { generate(prefix?: string): string }; type RetryPolicy = { name: string; maxRetries: number; baseDelayMs: number; factor: number; maxDelayMs: number; jitter: 'full' | 'none' }; StreamHandle.resume(resumeToken?: string). Promises and async iterators supported.
- Go: package ids: func GenerateIdempotencyKey(prefix string) string; type RetryPolicy struct { Name string; MaxRetries int; BaseDelay time.Duration; Factor float64; MaxDelay time.Duration; Jitter string } StreamResumer interface with Resume(ctx, token) (Stream, error).

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- Long-running streams: resumption windows are small by default (60s). For customers needing longer retention we'll provide an enterprise flag (server retention) and guidance to use server-side durable sessions.
- Non-idempotent backend actions: SDKs will not silently retry non-idempotent actions unless user provides an explicit idempotency key and opts into the appropriate policy. Default behavior for non-idempotent endpoints is fail-fast with guidance in docs.
- Clock skew: because idempotency key encodes timestamp, servers MUST be tolerant to reasonable clock skew (+/- 5 minutes). SDKs include optional clock-sync check and warn in logs if system time is off.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec reviewed and approved by SDK leads (Python/TS/Go) and Platform runtime lead.
- Implemented helpers and presets in Python/TS/Go SDKs with unit tests and integration tests using the local-resume test harness.
- Documented examples for: (a) chat UI using interactive preset; (b) background job with conservative preset and unary idempotency key; (c) resumable file-upload-like stream using resume tokens.
- Performance regression: default interactive retry profile does not increase median P50 latency by >5% for normal traffic (dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.com/sdks/retries/p95 over the smoke test harness).

Deliverables and artifacts:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123 (core API + tests)
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Interactive+Stream+Retry+Contract
- Resume test harness: https://qa.redwood.com/job/stream-resume-harness

Migration notes for customers:
- Existing consumers using ad-hoc idempotency keys should map keys to the new format and verify server TTL expectations. Migration helper scripts will be included in the SDK tools package.

Notes on security/compliance:
- Idempotency keys are non-secret. Do not place PII in keys. SDKs will redacted keys in logs by default.

QA checklist:
- Unit tests for key generation and TTL parsing (all languages)
- E2E tests for stream resume in both success and partial-output cases
- Chaos tests that inject connection resets at different offsets and verify dedup and resume behavior
- Telemetry events to track frequency of resumes and dedup hits

References:
- Related server work: ENG-87331 (server-side resume), ENG-70299 (session retention policy)
- Backoff/jitter patterns: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/exponential-backoff-and-jitter/
comments: 2026-03-02 - Design sync: Went over three retry profiles. PM (Sofia Patel) prefers interactive default for chat SDKs but asked for explicit opt-out that platform teams can enforce.

2026-03-03 - Engineering review: Discussed resume token security and agreed resume tokens are opaque server-issued strings; SDKs will treat them as unstructured tokens and persist them only in-memory unless user explicitly stores them.
2026-03-04 - Trade-off note: We debated storing TTL only on server; decided embedded timestamp in key is useful for quick gateway heuristics and offline debugging.
2026-03-05 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123 with Python helpers and initial tests. Requesting review from @noah-wilson and @sophia-kg.
2026-03-08 - Performance check: smoke harness shows interactive profile adds +2% median latency under 50 concurrent simulated chat sessions. Acceptable per acceptance criteria.
2026-03-09 - Feedback from TS lead (Marcus Lee): suggested naming change from 'resumable' to 'session-resume' for clarity. Patch incoming. Also requested stronger Typescript types for RetryPolicy.
2026-03-10 - Blocking tasks: Need integration test against staging runtime (ENG-87331) before merging. Assigned to Liam for follow-up.
2026-03-10 - Next steps: finalize docs on Confluence, follow-up PRs for TS/Go SDKs, add examples to quickstart templates.
